news.content: Americas Uruguay declares health emergency for avian influenza Authorities restrict poultry movement, suspend public events following detection of H5 virus Muhammed Yasin Güngör 05 September 2026 • Update : 05 September 2026 İSTANBUL Uruguay declared a nationwide health emergency on Friday after the discovery of the highly pathogenic H5 avian influenza in backyard poultry, according to officials. The Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries Ministry, through the General Directorate of Livestock Services, confirmed the outbreak in Colonia, a department in the southwest. That was after a health concern triggered by bird mortality. Although an initial rapid test yielded negative results, subsequent official laboratory analysis confirmed the presence of the virus. Authorities ordered a nationwide "interdiction of the affected establishment" alongside strict movement restrictions on non-commercial birds. The emergency directive restricts all domestic movement of backyard and uncontrolled birds, while exempting those registered under the official Poultry Monitoring System. The resolution also suspends fairs, auctions and public exhibitions related to avian species. Authorities ordered that free-range and backyard poultry must be confined to "enclosed, covered facilities" to prevent contact with wild birds. Sanitarians have initiated the slaughter and safe disposal of all exposed birds at the affected site, alongside extensive cleaning and disinfection of potentially contaminated materials. For poultry producers, the ministry recommended "extreme "biosecurity measures, such as restricting the entry of unauthorized people or vehicles, protecting water and food sources from wild birds, and reinforcing disinfection protocols. Officials emphasized that consuming poultry meat or eggs does not pose any risk to human health, though agricultural teams are coordinating with health authorities to monitor exposed individuals. Avian influenza A(H5N1), a highly pathogenic subtype that primarily infects birds but can rarely transmit to humans via close contact, carries a high mortality rate in humans, though sustained human-to-human transmission has not been recorded. The public is urged not to handle dead or sick birds. supplementary_news.content: 顶部 首页 首页 晴 / 20° STTT | 中国医学科学院王佑春/鲁帅尧/中国药品生物制品检定所黄维金/聂建辉团队研发高效鼻内H5N1疫苗 病毒学界 高致病性H5N1禽流感病毒跨物种传播能力突出,感染人体后死亡率极高,现有疫苗平台应对这一病毒时存在研发周期长、扩产困难以及难以激发足够细胞免疫反应的短板。2026年9月9日,中国医学科学院王佑春、鲁帅尧,中国药品生物制品检定所黄维金、聂建辉团队在《Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy》期刊发表了题为“Highly efficient intranasal H5N1 vaccine based on a safe vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) vector” 的研究论文。研究团队基于自主构建的高表达6-9G重组VSV载体,在M基因中引入Δ51联合S226R位点突变,获得了安全性显著提升且免疫原性优良的减毒载体,并基于该载体构建了H5N1候选疫苗,经两剂鼻内免疫后可诱导持久的体液和黏膜免疫应答,在小鼠模型中实现了100%的攻毒保护。 研究团队首先在6-9G载体基础上构建了M基因突变系列载体,包括6-9G-Δ51、6-9G-Δ51+V221F和6-9G-Δ51+S226R。体外复制动力学实验显示,在干扰素信号完整的PC3细胞中这些突变株复制速度减慢,但在干扰素缺陷的Vero细胞中它们的滴度均高于对照载体pr-VSV-G-GFP,其中6-9G-Δ51+S226R在感染后24小时的滴度较对照提升了44.9倍。体内安全评价中,通过脑内注射攻毒后6-9G-Δ51+S226R组的半数致死量(LD50)达到了6.9×106 FFU,是6-9G组的19714倍,该组小鼠脑组织病毒载量较pr-VSV-G-GFP组降低了17.2倍,鼻内接种后肺组织病毒载量也较对照组下降了5.9倍。 展开剩余 56 % 在免疫原性评估中,研究团队比较了肌肉、皮内、皮下、腹腔、尾静脉和鼻内六种接种途径,结果显示鼻内途径在免疫后第7天即可在血清中检测到中和抗体,应答速度最快。随后以鼻内途径接种1×106 FFU的各载体后动态监测至第49天,6-9G-Δ51+S226R组诱导的中和抗体水平持续攀升且滴度显著高于其他突变组。通过蛋白质组学比较分析6-9G和6-9G-Δ51+S226R感染小鼠的脑组织,共鉴定出944个差异表达蛋白,基因集富集分析显示钙信号通路和神经受体-配体相互作用通路在6-9G组中显著上调,而6-9G-Δ51+S226R组的NF-κB通路关键分子如CD40、Plcg2、Tradd和Rela表达水平更高,ISG通路基因如Ifh1和Lgp1c等也呈现出明显的组间差异。 基于安全性最优的6-9G-Δ51+S226R骨架,研究团队用H5N1毒株F3SM281(clade 2.3.4.4b)的HA和NA基因替换了VSV的G基因,获得了候选疫苗6-9GΔ51+S226R-H5N1。该疫苗在Vero细胞中的复制峰值为107 FFU/ml,低于亲本载体约两个数量级,脑内注射后LD50超过5×106 FFU,较亲本载体提升了10倍以上。两剂鼻内免疫(105 FFU)后小鼠血清中和抗体滴度达到103~104,支气管肺泡灌洗液中检测到特异性IgA(滴度32~64),而肌肉注射重组HA蛋白的对照组未能诱导黏膜IgA。攻毒实验中疫苗组仅出现约5%的短暂体重下降,全部存活至第7天,肺部病毒载量较PBS组降低了约3~4个对数,鼻甲和气管组织降低了2~3个对数,肺组织病理学检查仅见轻微的支气管周围炎症细胞浸润。 在持久性评价中,106 FFU和105 FFU两个剂量组鼻内免疫后第250天血清中和抗体滴度分别维持在104和103水平,此时以10倍LD50剂量攻毒后两个剂量组和蛋白对照组均全部存活,而PBS组从第5天起出现死亡并在第6天全部死亡。第7天组织病毒载量检测显示三个疫苗组肺部病毒载量较PBS组降低约1个对数,但鼻甲和气管组织降低约5个对数,组织病理学检查显示106 FFU组几乎未见明显病理改变。该疫苗骨架结合了Kozak序列以提升外源基因表达效率,在Vero细胞中可实现高效扩增,为H5N1及其他高致病性病原体的快速疫苗开发提供了具备产业转化潜力的技术平台。 Free web novels for online reading. 评论 全部 还没有人评论过,快来抢首评 抢首评 推荐阅读 温碧霞本色出演,堪称颜值巅峰之作,看得热血沸腾 文娱江湖 Meeting Request Archives SDPB App Boards & Commissions Unified Judicial System South Dakota Legislature Business & Economics Several new bird flu outbreaks reported in South Dakota flocks SDPB | By SDPB News Staff Published September 10, 2026 at 4:45 PM CDT File Health officials are confirming several new avian flu outbreaks at commercial flocks in South Dakota. The most recent outbreaks were reported Sept. 9 and impacted commercial turkey flocks at two South Dakota operations, according to the USDA. One outbreak in Turner County affected over 43,000 birds, and another in McPherson County impacted over 61,000. Another outbreak was reported Sept. 4 at a commercial breeder operation in Edmunds County affecting 30,000 birds. It’s standard practice to euthanize the entire flock once the disease is detected to prevent it from spreading, health officials say. These latest outbreaks come after the USDA reported four outbreaks in South Dakota throughout August that collectively affected roughly 150,000 birds. The federal Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service tracks detections nationwide. In the past four years there have been outbreaks detected in nearly 150 flocks in South Dakota involving more than eight million birds. Bailey Pemberton Fri, September 4, 2026 at 11:18 PM CDT 2 min read MRNA +0.74% Moderna (NasdaqGS:MRNA) has started a Phase 3 trial of its mRNA based bird flu vaccine, moving the program into late stage testing. The trial is supported by a major international partnership focused on pandemic preparedness. Moderna has tied the program to commitments for equitable global access, including reserved manufacturing capacity for low and middle income countries. This push into mRNA vaccines for emerging infectious diseases points to a wider theme in healthcare that is worth exploring through 37 healthcare AI stocks. NasdaqGS:MRNA Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Sep 2026 Moderna is a US based biotechnology company that develops messenger RNA medicines across infectious disease and other therapeutic areas, and it now has a market value of about $59.4b. This bird flu program sits within its broader effort to apply the same mRNA platform across multiple global health threats. We've flagged 1 risk for Moderna. See which could impact your investment. What Moderna's bird flu trial really changes for its mRNA Narrative For investors, the Phase 3 bird flu trial slots directly into Moderna's Narrative around expanding the mRNA pipeline beyond COVID, but it does not remove the key risks. It supports the catalyst that regulators and global health partners see Moderna as a rapid response partner for pandemic preparedness, which can create more stable government and advance purchase channels for vaccines. At the same time, the need for external support and prior use of sizeable 2032 convertible notes underline the Narrative concern about limited internal capital flexibility and the importance of careful portfolio prioritisation. If we take a look at the community Narrative for Moderna, we can see how this news fits into the bigger investment story. From here, one practical marker to watch is the actual scale and timing of any government or multilateral purchase commitments that follow this Phase 3 program, particularly volumes linked to declared pandemic scenarios and the pledged 20% manufacturing allocation for low and middle income countries. That will show how much this late stage trial and CEPI's US$54 million support convert into tangible, contracted demand alongside Moderna's broader respiratory and infectious disease plans. supplementary_news.content: News World Uruguay declares emergency over bird flu — Anadolu Agency UA.NEWS 05 September 2026 05:09 Uruguay has declared a nationwide public health emergency after highly pathogenic H5 avian influenza was detected in backyard poultry in the Colonia department in the country’s southwest. The outbreak was confirmed by the Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries through the General Directorate of Veterinary Services. Concerns arose after birds died: the initial rapid test was negative, but a subsequent official laboratory analysis confirmed the presence of the virus, Anadolu Agency reports . Restrictions on poultry movement Authorities banned operations at the affected farm and introduced strict restrictions on the movement of non-commercial poultry. The decision also limits the domestic movement of backyard and unregulated birds, except for those registered in the official poultry monitoring system. The country has suspended fairs, auctions and public exhibitions involving birds. Free-range and backyard poultry must be kept in enclosed covered facilities to prevent contact with wild birds. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . Biosecurity measures Veterinary services have begun the culling and safe disposal of all birds exposed at the affected facility. Thorough cleaning and disinfection of materials that may have been contaminated are also being carried out. Poultry producers were advised to strengthen biosecurity measures: restrict access for outsiders and vehicles, protect water and feed from wild birds, and enhance disinfection protocols. Officials stressed that consuming poultry meat and eggs poses no risk to human health. Agricultural services are coordinating with health authorities to monitor people who may have been exposed to the virus. Avian influenza A(H5N1) mainly affects birds, but in rare cases can be transmitted to humans through close contact. Citizens were urged not to touch sick or dead birds. News Reps urge USTR to press China on bird flu regionalization House members note China’s inconsistent enforcement of Regionalization Agreement costs U.S. chicken producers $800M annually. National Chicken Council September 8, 2026 schedule2 Min Read Getty Images A bipartisan group of more than two dozen House members sent a letter on Aug. 28 to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer urging continued pressure on China to fully comply with the U.S.-China HPAI Regionalization Agreement. The letter, signed by 29 lawmakers, representing a majority of the districts that have production and are impacted by the highly pathogenic avian influenza bans, thanked Ambassador Greer for prioritizing chicken market access in recent negotiations with China but pressed for further action to remove remaining restrictions on U.S. chicken exports. Background The letter traces the dispute back to a March 2020 Regionalization Agreement, part of the Phase One Trade Agreement, which was designed to limit trade disruptions from HPAI detections by imposing only statewide (rather than nationwide) bans, with resumption of trade 90 days after virus elimination. While China initially followed those terms after the 2022 HPAI outbreak began, the General Administration of Customs China (GACC) reinstated broader bans in August 2022. By April 2026, 44 states were ineligible to export raw chicken to China — representing nearly 98 percent of registered U.S. chicken facilities. Related:AI helps researchers target bacteria behind beef browning Following President Trump’s May 2026 visit to China, GACC agreed to resume imports from HPAI-free states as designated by [the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Animal & Plant Health Inspection Service], lifting restrictions on 17 states. However, the lawmakers note China has not adhered to the agreed five-business-day window for lifting restrictions after receiving APHIS closeout reports. As of August 2026, 21 states remain banned, representing 34 percent of U.S. chicken production, though the letter acknowledges GACC recently lifted restrictions for eight additional states. Why it matters China’s inconsistent enforcement of the Regionalization Agreement has significantly constrained one of the U.S. chicken industry’s most valuable export markets, particularly for paws and dark meat cuts with limited domestic demand. As recently as 2022, China was the second-largest export market for U.S. chicken, with more than 622,000 metric tons valued at over $1.1 billion. By 2025, shipments had fallen to just 93,978 metric tons valued at $291 million. The letter estimates China’s noncompliance with HPAI regionalization and relisting terms is costing American chicken producers more than $800 million annually. NCC’s take The National Chicken Council strongly welcomes this bipartisan letter and shares the lawmakers’ frustration with China’s inconsistent adherence to the HPAI Regionalization Agreement. We appreciate USTR’s work securing the recent state relistings and echo the letter’s call for continued, sustained pressure on Beijing to honor its commitments. NCC will continue working with USTR, USDA and Congress to press for full restoration of market access for all eligible states. Related:Meat Institute concerned by Trump’s order to explore beef origin labeling What’s next The letter identifies Iowa, Maryland, North Carolina, Pennsylvania and South Carolina as states expected to soon meet the Regionalization Agreement’s provisions for lifted restrictions, pending no additional HPAI detections and timely Chinese action on APHIS closeout reports. Lawmakers are urging USTR to continue raising the issue with Chinese counterparts at every opportunity. supplementary_news.content: 9月10日 23:25 星期四 🌦️奥克兰 14°C 小雨 繁 搜索 × 首页新西兰财经房产移民教育国际人物旅游汽车生活娱乐体育专题视频先驱文苑先驱报电子版 搜索 × 繁 首页新西兰财经房产移民教育国际人物旅游汽车生活娱乐体育专题视频先驱文苑先驱报电子版联系我们广告服务关于我们隐私政策使用条款 警报拉响!致命H5N1禽流感首次进入悉尼! By 新西兰中文先驱网· 2026年09月07日 18:15 澳洲禽流感 分享 听新闻▶0:00/0:00✕ 顶部 来源:悉尼印象 致命的H5N1禽流感病毒正在全球范围内导致鸟类和海豹种群数量锐减,如今该病毒已在悉尼被检测到。 新州政府确认,在Port Kembla和悉尼北部海滩地区的Warriewood,两只凤头燕鸥检测出H5N1禽流感病毒呈阳性。 第三宗病例也在Coffs Harbour的Corindi被确认,感染对象是一只哈顿氏剪水鹱。 北部海滩地区的两宗病例,是悉尼市区范围内首次记录到H5N1禽流感病毒;而Coffs Harbour的病例,则是新州首次确认在剪水鹱中发现该病毒。 周五,一名政府发言人表示,目前当地没有出现大规模鸟类死亡的迹象,相关监测工作仍在持续。 截至周四,新州共发现20起H5型禽流感事件,全国范围内则达到468起。 新州环境部长Penny Sharpe表示,政府对这种病毒可能对该州野生动物造成的影响“深感担忧”。 她表示:“任何政府政策都无法阻止这种病毒在我们的野生鸟类种群中传播。” “我们能够采取的措施,是为具有重要保护价值的种群接种疫苗、保护它们的栖息地,并清除入侵物种。” “公众同样发挥着重要作用,应避免接触生病或死亡的鸟类,并向动物疾病紧急热线报告,帮助我们发现新的病例,并有针对性地开展监测工作。” 新州农业部长Tara Moriarty表示,政府目前仍将重点放在“做好准备、开展监测以及迅速应对相关事件”上。 她表示:“现在,所有在后院饲养鸡只或在鸟舍中饲养宠物鸟的人,都应该采取预防措施,确保自家鸡只和宠物鸟不会与野生鸟类发生接触。” “政府还建议,人们在海滩或公园遛狗时要格外小心,确保宠物不会啃食动物尸体或追逐野生鸟类。” “接触病毒的风险较低,但降低宠物面临的任何风险都非常重要。” 目前,家禽养殖业仍仅采取自愿性的家禽圈养建议,并非强制执行。 当局呼吁居民通过动物疾病紧急热线,对死亡、生病或濒死的鸟类进行拍照并报告。 相关阅读: 澳大利亚确认首例哺乳动物感染H5N1禽流感病例 新西兰发现第三例H5禽流感病例 做好准备!墨尔本鸡蛋可能要吃不上了,价格也可能飙升。政府紧急要求:养鸡场快把鸡关起来,别乱跑 新州致命禽流感疫情持续扩散,本土鸟类首次确诊!全澳确诊总数升至215例 H5禽流感在澳扩散,海滩现大量死鸟,专家忧心“进入下一阶段” 为防禽流感,55万只散养鸡进入封闭管理,超市呼吁勿抢购囤积 新西兰确认第二例H5N1禽流感!本土鸟类中招,家禽业高度戒备! 禽流感病例首现,专家警告这类物种面临巨大风险!环保部正在行动! 新西兰确诊首例H5禽流感病例!鸡蛋要涨价了? supplementary_news.content: Tiếng Việt 首页 话题 时事 政治制度 当地的 事件 旅游 快乐越南 企业 产品 遗产 博物馆 数字 多媒体 数据 时事 文化 - 社会 Thuc Phan Ward 正在紧急隔离和控制 A/H5N1 禽流感疫情。 9月6日,Thuc Phan 区采取措施隔离和处理疫情,销毁了黄松住宅区感染A/H5N1的家禽群;开展卫生消毒工作,并积极控制该地区疾病的传播。 Báo Cao Bằng•07/09/2026 Google Google 0 Khám phá thêm Điểm đến du lịch Tin tức Tham khảo Địa lý 此前,9月1日,宿务市叔潘坊黄松住宅区爆发甲型H5N1禽流感疫情。经送检,中央兽医诊断检测中心1号分中心检测,黄松住宅区黎光沙先生家鸭子的样本呈甲型H5N1禽流感病毒阳性。该家鸭群约有3000只。 利用洪水打造的创意空间。曾经被视为废弃物的、被洪水冲刷上来的浮木,在黎玉顺的巧手和创意下,变成了创造独特创意空间的材料。 创造创意空间能够丰富城市文化生活。在文化产业、创意经济和知识经济日益成为许多国家发展的重要驱动力的背景下,创意空间不再仅仅指物理场所。在发达城市,设计创意空间是一种支持创意过程、促进创新以及连接人、思想、技术和社会资源的策略。 永光乡居民的两项职业培训课程已经开课。(GLO)——9月10日,嘉莱省职业教育和继续教育中心与永光乡文化社会事务部合作,为当地居民组织了两个职业培训班的开班仪式,每个班级招收35名学生。 Thuc Phan 区当局在 Hoang Tung 住宅区收集了感染禽流感 A/H5N1 的家禽,并按照规定对其进行了销毁。 疫情爆发后,区人民委员会立即组织扑杀了全部鸭群,总重5363公斤,并按照规定掩埋,以消除病源,限制病毒传播到环境和邻近畜牧区的风险;同时向居民组提供了125公斤石灰和消毒化学品,用于卫生、消毒和灭菌。 区人民委员会指示专门力量加强对畜禽疫情的审查和监测,及时发现病死禽禽;监测疫情发展,采取措施隔离控制疫情,并在疫情控制后控制禽禽的补栏。要求养殖户严格遵守疫情防控规定;发现禽禽出现异常症状时,必须向地方主管部门报告,不得出售、运输、屠宰或食用病死禽禽。 农历九月十一日 - supplementary_news.content: Latest News Syria Middle East Economy Politics Sport International Reading: Canberra study tracks migratory birds to map H5N1 spread in Australia AR TR FR ES KU Latest News Syria Middle East Economy Politics Sport International Reading: Canberra study tracks migratory birds to map H5N1 spread in Australia AR TR FR ES KU Culture Video Photos Miscellaneous Latest News Syria Middle East Economy Politics Sport International Search Latest News News Categories Politics Culture Video Photos Miscellaneous Provinces Languages العربية Türkçe Français Español Kurdî Follow US Canberra study tracks migratory birds to map H5N1 spread in Australia Published: 2026/09/07 1:45 PM Updated: 2026/09/07 1:48 PM A massive flock of snow geese taking flight against a clear blue sky in Tennessee. Photo: Birdfact Canberra, Sept. 07 (SANA) Australian researchers are using migratory bird tracking data to model the potential spread of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza and identify species and areas that could face greater infection risks, according to a Phys.org report published Sunday. Researchers at Deakin University have studied the movements of migratory shorebirds for years, using tracking data in models designed to help predict how the virus could spread across Australia, the report said. Wild birds can carry the virus over long distances, making information about migration routes and gathering sites an important indicator of areas the virus could potentially reach. Some species face greater infection risks, particularly seabirds living in colonies and species that feed in water where they may come into contact with droppings from other birds. Birds of prey, crows and magpies may also be exposed when approaching sick or dead birds. The impact of H5N1 is not limited to birds. Large-scale deaths among some marine mammals have been reported in South America, while deaths among seals and dolphins have been recorded in Australia, underscoring the importance of monitoring the virus across wildlife species. Deaths among great crested terns have provided researchers with another indicator for tracking the virus’s arrival among local species after infections were detected in seabirds that rarely reach mainland Australia. Researchers said community participation could strengthen surveillance, particularly along Australia’s extensive coastline, where comprehensive monitoring is difficult. Reports of sick or dead birds can provide useful data for tracking potential virus spread. They urged members of the public not to touch sick or dead birds and to report them to the appropriate authorities, allowing trained teams to handle the animals safely, conduct testing and monitor possible signs of virus transmission. Tracking bird movements and reporting wildlife sickness or deaths provide scientists with important tools for monitoring the potential spread of H5N1 and assessing associated risks. supplementary_news.content: ___ × Market Information Top Poultry Companies Expert Insights Blogs Regions Magazines Sign In Poultry Meat Egg Poultry Health Sustainability Poultry Future Chicken Marketing Summit Poultry Tech Summit Broilers & Turkeys Diseases & Health Avian Influenza Two South Dakota turkey flocks hit by avian flu A total of 105,100 birds are lost in the two latest flock infections. Roy Graber September 10, 2026 Farm & Food Care Article Summary Two commercial turkey flocks in South Dakota were confirmed to have highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) on September 9, affecting over 105,000 birds combined. South Dakota has been hit hardest by the outbreak this year, with six flocks affected since August 12 and a total of 16 commercial poultry flocks lost to HPAI in 2026. Two flocks confirmed: McPherson County (61,300 birds) and Turner County (43,800 birds) both tested positive for HPAI on September 9. South Dakota hardest hit: The state has lost 6 flocks since August 12 across McPherson, Turner, Hamlin, Beadle, and Edmunds counties. 2026 total impact: South Dakota has recorded 16 commercial poultry flocks lost to avian flu this year, with 284,000 birds affected across all six fall outbreak flocks. Regional spread: North Dakota and Minnesota also confirmed HPAI in commercial poultry this fall, though South Dakota remains the most affected state. Two more commercial meat turkey flocks in South Dakota have been hit by highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI). The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) reported that both cases were confirmed on September 9. One flock was in McPherson County and involved 61,300 birds. The other flock was in Turner County and involved 43,800 birds. So far this fall, three states have had the presence of HPAI confirmed in commercial poultry, with North Dakota and Minnesota being the other two. However, it is South Dakota that has been hit the hardest. The state has had six flocks affected since August 12. Two of those flock infections were in Edmunds County, while the counties of McPherson, Turner, Hamlin and Beadle have each had one flock affected. Collectively, those flocks included 284,000 birds. To date in 2026, South Dakota has lost 16 commercial poultry flocks to HPAI. To learn more about HPAI cases in commercial poultry flocks in the United States, Mexico and Canada, see an interactive map on WATTPoultry.com. Jackie Linden September 8, 2026 Roy Graber | DALL-E Article Summary Bulgaria and France confirmed their first highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks of fall 2024 in late August, with the H5N1 virus detected in commercial duck flocks that resulted in hundreds of bird deaths across both countries. Bulgaria and France each reported their first H5N1 avian flu cases of the fall season in late August 2024 France detected the virus in a flock of 7,600 ducks in Maine-et-Loire with approximately 150 birds dead; Bulgaria reported 260 deaths in a 14,000-duck flock So far this year, 313 avian flu outbreaks have been confirmed in commercial poultry farms across 16 European countries, with Poland leading at 143 cases Wild bird migrations entering fall season are increasing the risk of H5N1 transmission to domestic flocks, with 2,681 wild bird cases detected across Europe year-to-date France has maintained a mandatory vaccination program for commercial ducks against H5N1 since October 2023 In the last two days of August, veterinary agencies in Bulgaria and France confirmed their nation’s first highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreaks of the fall. The presence of the H5N1 virus variant was confirmed after around 150 birds died out of the flock of around 7,600 ducks in the French department of Maine-et-Loire, around 200km southwest of Paris. According to the official notification from the authorities to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), the birds had previously been vaccinated. A state-wide HPAI vaccination scheme has been in place in France since October of 2023. This has involved — and been limited to — the mandatory vaccination of commercial ducks against the H5N1 HPAI virus serotype. So far, the agriculture ministry has not announced details of a similar campaign starting next month. Since the season’s first outbreak at the end of August, the ministry reports that the HPAI virus has been detected at a further two commercial poultry premises in Maine-et-Loire, which is part of the Pays de la Loire region in western France. Following a period of five months without new cases in poultry, the Bulgarian animal health agency notified WOAH about the detection of the H5N1 HPAI virus in a flock of 14,000 mallard ducks at the end of August. Around 260 of the birds are reported to have died as a result of the infection. The affected premises is located in the central province of Plovdiv. Overview of HPAI in European domestic flocks In the past two weeks, the H5N1 HPAI virus has been detected in just two poultry flocks in Europe — one in each of Bulgaria and France. These bring to 313 the number of outbreaks on commercial farms in 16 countries in the region so far this year, according to the European Commission (EC; as of September 2). EC’s Animal Disease Information System database monitors listed animal diseases in European Union member states and selected adjacent countries. At each location, presence of the H5N1 virus variant has been confirmed. For comparison, 729 outbreaks in these flocks were reported by 23 countries during the whole of 2025. This year, Poland’s total remains unchanged but the highest to date at 143. Next come Germany (40), France (21) and Italy (19). In a separate category of “captive birds,” the EC System tracks HPAI outbreaks involving backyard poultry, ornamental flocks, zoos and similar premises. With no new cases in the past six weeks or so, the category total remains stable at 119 outbreaks in 15 countries so far this year. During the whole of 2025, 25 countries registered with the EC a total of 175 outbreaks involving captive birds. 4 countries confirm new H5N1 cases in wild birds As Europe enters meteorological autumn/fall, wild bird migrations start to pick up, increasing the risk of HPAI infections in both wild and domestic bird species. Since mid-August, the number of new detections of H5N1 variant in the wild population has increased by just nine — six in Norway, and one in each of Denmark, the Netherlands, and Portugal. These bring the outbreak total in Europe’s wild population for the year to date to 2,681 (as of September 2) across 32 countries in the region. In more than 2,640 of these outbreaks, the H5N1 serotype was identified, while the others also involved an H5 virus. Last year, 4,751 HPAI outbreaks in this population were logged with the EC’s System by 34 countries. In its latest assessment for the HPAI situation in Germany, the national veterinary reference laboratory Friedrich-Loeffler Institute (FLI) has raised the risk level to “moderate” for the transmission of the virus to and within the country’s wild bird population. Meanwhile, the chances of infection in Germany’s commercial poultry and captive birds, and undetected infections in waterfowl flocks are considered to remain low, according to FLI.
